correctness.rationale: The frozen count itself is correct: for fixed diagonal pair, one arrow has q² solutions exactly when both labels agree at its endpoints and q otherwise, including q² for a loop. Expanding the product and dividing by the appropriate group orders proves all three formulas. The repair keeps and checks the separate orientation counterexample. The unique Sylow p-subgroup (C_p)^3 is characteristic and its conjugation action factors through the diagonal quotient. Any abstract isomorphism would induce an F_p-linear intertwiner after a quotient isomorphism, so it would preserve the relation kernel among the three distinct one-dimensional characters up to permutation. The cycle requires x=y=z, whereas the transitive triangle requires x=y=−z; these subgroups differ for p≥5. The repaired full-spectrum equality follows from the cited theorem and its direct specialization: radical conjugation contributes p^(3−|B|), and the torus orbit of a surviving support F has size (p−1)^(3−k(F)); the quotient of the number of support vectors by this orbit size is direction independent. For p=5 the three diagonal types contribute 44, 72 and 24 classes, giving 140 of group order 8000 and probability 7/400.
residual_risks: The nonisomorphism comparison uses prime fields of characteristic at least five. The legacy checker does not test group isomorphism or entire conjugacy spectra; the repaired claims use the symbolic argument.

value.rationale: The surviving claim shows on a canonical three-vertex graph, uniformly over the stated prime fields, that even all conjugacy-class sizes with multiplicities cannot recover the abstract group. The quotient action identifies exactly what the class-size data miss in this example: the signed relation between the three weights. This distinction is stronger and more useful than reproducing an aggregate count or comparing the underlying algebras, neither of which is asserted as new in the repair.
residual_risks: The example does not classify arbitrary orientations or show that character-relation kernels suffice for arbitrary groups.
